info.title: MonitorFlow public API
info.description: Scripts and integrations use `/api/v1` with an API key made under Admin › API keys: `Authorization: Bearer mfk_…`. A key acts as the administrator who made it, within its reach (everything, a customer or a site), its access and its areas. Lists that can grow take `limit` and `cursor` and answer `next_cursor`, null on the last page. Every error has `error`, plain words, and `code`, stable. Writes may carry `Idempotency-Key`; the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. A key makes up to 600 requests a minute; answers carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`, and 429 carries `Retry-After`. See ADR-0101.

403.description: The key's role or areas do not allow it: `forbidden` or `api_key_scope`

404.description: Not found, or outside the key's reach: `not_found`

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`

post.description:
What the classifier would decide for `command` on the servers of a
site (built-in rules, then the customer's and the site's rules), or
with the customer-wide rules only when `site_id` is null. A dry run:
nothing is stored, logged or sent to an agent. `shell` is `posix` for
Linux servers, `powershell` for Windows ones.

The answer's `tier` is what would happen: `read_only` runs at once,
`low_impact` waits for an approver unless the site's policy lets it
run, `high_impact` waits for an administrator, `forbidden` never runs.

Needs any role on the customer as a whole and the key area
"remediation". Safe to repeat.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer instead of running twice.

get.description:
The remediation audit log: the events of every remediation incident on
the sites the caller reads, newest first, across incidents. Each event
carries its incident's customer, site, server, metric and instance.
`payload` leaves out the context sent to the AI (`context.rendered`)
and command output (`stdout`, `stderr`); read the incident for them
and to verify its chain.

Needs any role and the key area "remediation". Filters are ANDed; a
filter outside the caller's sites gives an empty list. Paginated with
`limit` and `cursor`; unknown parameters and bad values are 400.

get.description:
What the AI did about alerts: one remediation incident per alert it
worked on, newest `opened_at` first. Read-only: the remediation loop
opens, drives and closes them. An incident in `awaiting_approval`
carries the command waiting for a person in `pending_command`; the
approval queue (`/remediation/approvals`) decides it.

Needs any role and the key area "remediation"; lists the incidents of
the servers of the sites the caller reads. A filter outside them gives
an empty list. Paginated with `limit` and `cursor`; unknown parameters
and bad values are 400.

put.description:
Sets whether low-impact commands run without approval on the servers
of a customer (`site_id` null) or of one of its sites. With `true`,
the next low-impact commands the AI proposes there are approved by
MonitorFlow itself and sent to the agent at once; commands already
waiting for approval still wait. It never lets high-impact commands
run on their own. An agent runs AI commands only when its own
administrator allowed them on the server (ADR-0098).

Needs an administrator role on the customer as a whole and the key
area "remediation". Audited as `remediation_policy.update`. Safe to
repeat: it sets the value.

post.description:
Adds an administrator rule to the classifier of a customer, or of one
of its sites. It applies to the next command the AI proposes on the
servers it covers; nothing is sent to agents. A command already waiting
for approval keeps its tier, but is classified again when approved.

- `allow`: a command no built-in rule knows, matching `pattern` as a
  whole, gets `tier`, `read_only` (runs without approval) or
  `low_impact` (needs approval unless the site's policy lets it run).
  An allow rule never applies to a command a built-in rule decides,
  and its program may not be one the built-in rules reserve (`sudo`,
  shells and interpreters, package managers, `systemctl`, `rm`,
  `kill`, `reboot` and the like): that is 400.
- `deny`: a command containing a match anywhere, after `;`, `&&`, `|`
  too, is `forbidden`, whatever the other rules say. Deny wins over
  every allow rule.
- `cache_dir`: `find <pattern> -mindepth 1 -delete` becomes a
  low-impact command for that directory.

Needs an administrator role on the customer as a whole and the key
area "remediation". Audited as `remediation_rule.create`. Not safe to
repeat with a different body; the same rule twice is 409.

with the rule's pattern. Deleting again is 404.

incident_ids.description: 1 to [`MAX_LIMIT`] incidents, like a group of a notification.

note.description:
What the user is doing about them, up to 500 characters, shown with
the acknowledgement (ADR-0130). Required when signed in; optional
for API keys, so older scripts keep working.

Acknowledged.description:
Body of the answer: the incidents this request acknowledged. The
others were resolved, or someone acknowledged them first.

AcknowledgementNote.description:
Who acknowledged a server's latest acknowledged open incident, when,
and what they said they are doing (ADR-0130).

note.description: `null` from a notification link or a script that sent none.

Aggregation.description: A simple aggregation across the selected series.

AiCommandsChange.description: The last `ai_commands` command of a server, in `GET /api/servers/{id}`.

requested_by.description: The username, `null` when the account is gone.

command.description: Runs this instead of the proposal, recorded as an `edit`.

reason.description: One sentence for the approval queue and the audit log.

rule.description:
The rule that decided: `{"source": "builtin", "id": "readonly.df"}`
or `{"source": "configured", "id": "<rule UUID>"}`.

oneOf.description: A built-in rule, by its stable ID such as `readonly.df`.

command.description:
The command line, as the AI would propose it. Neither stored nor
logged.

shell.description:
`posix` (the default) for Linux servers, `powershell` for Windows
ones (ADR-0084).

site_id.description:
The site whose rules apply as well; `null` or absent for the
customer-wide rules only.

CommandDetail.description:
`GET /api/commands/{id}`: the command and its output, each at most
the last 64 KiB.

health_timeout_s.description:
`self_update`: seconds the new agent has to connect before the
old one comes back; 30 to 3600, 300 by default.

packages.description: Packages to upgrade; empty or absent for all.

ttl_s.description:
Seconds the agent may still start it; [`MIN_TTL_S`] to
[`MAX_TTL_S`], default [`DEFAULT_TTL_S`].

parameters.description: The payload as JSON, for kinds the API knows.

site_count.description: Sites of the customer the user reads, not all of them.

command.description: What will run, or what was rejected.

details.description:
For instance `{"reason": "threshold_removed"}`, `{"notified":
true}` when a silence ended, `{"username", "via"}` when
acknowledged, or `{"step", "steps", "minutes", "told"}` for a
follow-up step.

kind.description:
`opened`, `escalated`, `deescalated`, `resolved`, what a silence
did: `silenced` and `silence_ended` (ADR-0079), `acknowledged`, and
`followed_up` when a follow-up step told someone (ADR-0082).

occurred_at.description: Sample time of the change, or the server clock without a sample.

severity.description: Severity after the change; `null` once resolved.

FollowUpView.description: Where an incident is in its follow-up.

next.description: Who it would tell then, people first; empty when nobody can be.

next_at.description: When the next step is told if nobody acknowledges.

started_at.description: When the first message went out.

state.description:
`waiting` for the next step at `next_at`, `silenced` until a silence
ends then waiting, or `stopped`.

step.description: Steps told so far, and how many there are now.

stop_reason.description:
When stopped: `acknowledged`, `resolved`, `not_critical`, or
`finished` once every step was told.

GroupView.description: A notification that told this incident with others (ADR-0080).

incidents.description:
How many incidents it told that the user may read, this one
included. Members on sites outside the user's scope are not counted.

GuestKind.description: What a Proxmox guest is, which picks its API path.

oneOf.description:
Who is told next if nobody acknowledges (ADR-0082); `null` when no
follow-up started: a warning, or not sent yet.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

IncidentView.description:
One incident. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

acknowledged_by.description:
Who said they are on it, and when (ADR-0082); `null` until someone
does. The name stays when the account is removed.

acknowledged_note.description:
What they said they are doing (ADR-0130); `null` from a
notification link, or from an API key that sent none.

can_acknowledge.description:
Whether the reader may acknowledge it: open, not acknowledged, and
the reader an operator or above of its site.

hostname.description: The server's hostname, or the relay's name.

instance.description: `""` for a series without an instance.

metric.description: `offline` when the server or relay stopped reporting (ADR-0072).

opened_at.description: Sample times, not the server clock.

peak_value.description: The worst value seen while open.

reason.description:
Why it opened, in one sentence: "9% available is below the
warning limit of 12%"; for a resolved incident, its peak.

relay_id.description: Set for a relay's offline incident only (ADR-0072).

severity.description: `warning` or `critical`; the last one while resolved.

silenced.description: Whether a silence ever held back a notification of it.

silenced_until.description:
While open and covered by a silence, when the last one ends
(ADR-0079).

threshold.description: The threshold as it was when the incident opened.

PendingView.description:
One command waiting for approval. Field names and types are part of
the API contract: add fields, never rename or remove them.

can_approve.description:
Whether the user may approve this command as proposed, and reject
it. UX hints: the decision routes check again.

command.description: The proposed command, exactly as it would run.

commands_run.description: Commands the incident ran so far, and its limit.

deadline.description:
`opened_at + max_duration_s`: the incident escalates then, and a
decision after it is 409.

tags.name: remediation
tags.description: What the AI did about alerts. Each remediation incident is one alert the AI worked on, with every step recorded in a hash chain: the context it was sent after redaction, its proposals, how the rules classified each command, who approved or rejected it, and what the agent ran and printed. Read-only, except the approval queue, where people decide the commands the rules parked for them. The AI's text is untrusted: show it as data. Needs the key area "remediation".

tags.name: metrics
tags.description: Metric queries built by MonitorFlow, never raw PromQL

tags.name: risk rules
tags.description: How MonitorFlow decides what an AI command may do. Every command the AI proposes is classified by rules, never by the AI: `read_only` runs at once, `low_impact` waits for a person with an approver role unless the site's policy lets it run on its own, `high_impact` waits for an administrator, and `forbidden` never runs and hands the incident to a person. Built-in rules cover the commands MonitorFlow knows; administrators add allow rules for other commands (read-only or low impact only), deny patterns that forbid commands, and cache directories that may be cleared, for a customer or one of its sites. Rules and policies need a role on the customer as a whole (everything, or the customer): a role on one site, or a key that reaches one site, sees none. They need the key area "remediation".
